claims.statement: The test-flow JSON contract is version 1 with optional name and conditions plus required non-empty measurements; the loader rejects malformed shape, types, empty lists, unknown metrics, and duplicate targets/readings, and resets the parsed spec on any load failure.

Flow component references use IComponentEngine::id(), not graph-node IDs, and the harness and panel resolve them by scanning live engines. CircuitRuntime allocates component IDs from a monotonic counter, and removing a live component does not renumber survivors. A project load resets the counter to 100, creates saved components through createComponent in file order, then raises the counter to the saved next_component_id if that is higher, so deleting or reordering components before a save can leave an old flow ID missing or bound to a different engine after reload.

Condition paths address serialize() JSON keys with dot and array-index syntax, and path discovery recursively exposes scalar leaves while preserving numeric/type applicability; the same resolved slot and arithmetic acceptance rules are shared by authoring, validation, and patching.

ValidateFlow is a read-only exhaustive preflight over every condition value and measurement reference; RunFlow invokes that same pass before producing rows, so a panel using ValidateFlow cannot accept a flow the harness rejects.

RunFlow rejects cyclic topology before rows, freezes targeted component baselines, runs the Cartesian product with the last condition varying fastest, and updates engines in graph order; fatal failures return zero rows and deserialization failures attempt rollback of targeted baselines.

The app panel is an authoring/orchestration caller: its effective spec is the draft when present otherwise the loaded file, discovery comes from live engine serialization, and preview, run, and save all consume the same spec rather than implementing a second contract.

The panel imposes a 10,000-row ceiling because the harness is synchronous and uncapped, snapshots every live engine before running, restores snapshots independently afterward, rewires inputs, and latches restoration failure until a circuit reload.

Circuit reload clears the Test Flow panel's restoration latch, result, and status while retaining the selected flow/draft for revalidation; flow-run UI state is not persisted in the project, and restored successful runs leave the project revision unchanged.
Non-measurable metrics produce invalid samples rendered as N/A and encoded as JSON null with a separate valid flag, while such samples do not fail an otherwise successful run.

Flow authoring uses a finite-number grammar and atomic sibling-temporary-file writes, while result export writes pretty JSON with a trailing newline and preserves the in-memory successful result when export fails.

The supported extension boundary keeps metrics, condition path rules, and UI-free authoring helpers in the test_flow library, with the widget driving those helpers rather than duplicating document or validation logic.
RunFlowWithinBoundary snapshots every non-null live engine with serialize() before running, and a snapshot exception returns SnapshotFailed without calling RunFlow.

RunFlowWithinBoundary calls RunFlow once and records an exception from it as ExecutionFailed, then restores every snapshot once by component ID, letting later restores run after a failure, always rewires inputs, and returns RestoreFailed with the run's result discarded when any restore failed.

RunFlow restores baselines only when a deserialization fails inside its row loop; after a successful sweep it returns without restoring, so the live engines keep the last row's swept values until the boundary restores them.
test_flow_run checks the required epoch before it parses any condition or measurement, and a mismatch returns the stale-epoch error without running the flow.

While the agent flow latch is set, test_flow_run returns an INTERNAL error carrying the latch message and the reload hint without parsing or running the sweep, and AgentApi::noteProjectReplaced clears the latch.

test_flow_run accepts at most four conditions and one to eight measurements, rejects unknown fields and non-finite values with INVALID_ARGUMENT, and rejects duplicate condition paths and duplicate measurement readings at the later entry.
test_flow_run refuses a sweep whose saturating row product exceeds 1000 rows before any snapshot is taken, and the error details carry the requested count and the limit.
A RestoreFailed outcome from test_flow_run latches the agent flow state, marks the project modified, and returns INTERNAL, while SnapshotFailed and ExecutionFailed return INTERNAL without latching.

Ordinary FlowResult errors from test_flow_run map to NOT_FOUND for missing components or ports, PARAM_REJECTED (the AgentErrorCode::ParamRejected wire code) for inapplicable paths, INVALID_ARGUMENT for metric, duplicate, shape, and type errors, and INTERNAL for cyclic graphs and deserialization failures.

A successful test_flow_run reply echoes the checked epoch with row_count and per-row condition values and metric samples, encodes a non-finite metric value as null, and marks a sample invalid only when the metric is NaN.
The panel refuses a snapshot failure without latching, and only a RestoreFailed outcome latches it, which stores the restore notice in the status.

The panel calls RunFlowWithinBoundary directly, and the agent tool calls it through the default value of its run-boundary seam, so both paths share snapshot, restore, rewire, and outcome classification.
